subject.title: Harden Program Manager behavioral evals and handoff safety

question: Should OpenClaw accept a scheduled Program Manager live-eval workflow that hydrates provider and Codex secrets by default, or should this PR be narrowed until an approved live lane exists?
rationale: The diff changes a CI secret boundary and adds new eval-control surfaces; automation can identify unsafe mechanics, but maintainers must decide whether this scheduled live-secret lane belongs in core.

options.title: Narrow Before Merge
options.body: Keep the useful contracts, static checks, telemetry helper, and tests while removing default scheduled live-secret execution until the live lane is separately approved and hardened.

options.title: Approve A Hardened Live Lane
options.body: Accept the live-eval direction only after owner approval, existing command wiring, pinned runtime images, safe env writes, and artifact-backed proof are all present.

options.title: Pause For Smaller PRs
options.body: Ask for a smaller static Program Manager eval hardening PR first and handle live workflow scheduling as a separate security-reviewed change.

recommendation.title: Narrow Before Merge
recommendation.body: Keep the useful contracts, static checks, telemetry helper, and tests while removing default scheduled live-secret execution until the live lane is separately approved and hardened.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a repository-wide scheduled secret-bearing CI decision, and steipete is the strongest explicit ownership signal from CONTRIBUTING and CODEOWNERS.
